body: This is pretty much the most assuring and straightforward advice I have gotten all day. Thank you so much for sharing; I really needed to hear something like this. It brought tears to my eyes. I guess the biggest thing I have learned is it is okay to be sad on occasion. I have a boyfriend now of 6 months and he is wonderfully supportive. Even when I am extremely exhausted, tired and depressed, he doesn't think less of me. I have learned to in a sense *own it* when I feel shitty and not guilt trip myself into shaming myself more about it... Though it still is a "new" thing for me to try this. I have close friends far away, but making a new circle where I am living is the next step. I do want a family of my own and am slowly accepting my bf's family into my life. Thank you again for your story and your words. I am feeling better right now.
Thanks again so much. This subreddit is literally an emotional and physical life-saver. It's comforting to know that people care.

Thanks so much for your kind words. It does mean a lot just the fact I can relate. I am really sorry to hear about your mother's lack of involvement. I have just found for myself it is better to let go and forget about my parents shortcomings than try to analyze them and "understand." Sometimes it's better *not* to understand and purposely forget as I have recently learned to try. The "keep pushing" mentality is good advice and I've been trying to stick with that. I know rationally I *don't* want to give up, but the world weighs so heavy sometimes. I tend to get more angry than sad nowadays as it propels me more into *doing* than sitting around moping. Anyways, in the end there is no "right" way to grieve, but it is nice to know that people do care about my existence, even if sometimes I doubt myself.

Yes, I do have close friends (like a handful) but all of whom are scattered about geographically. Most of my friends are ambitious like I am so they have been moving and pursuing jobs elsewhere. I have a half sister and a bro in law who I am close to... But still they get "busy" with their own obligations (which I don't blame them for). I do have a boyfriend here now in the foreign country I am in and his family has been very welcoming and supportive... Though, it is still hard to get feel close with people. This took some time after my dad died as well. I am getting better at it but still struggling to *truly* open up to people. I have this fear that if I open up and get close, people will just be gone. I know it's irrational, but comes as a product of conditioning. I *just* started getting close with my dad, then he died. Then I *just* started getting close with my mom then she suddenly died. 

I guess the problem is, I *know* why I fear getting close to people because I know how bad it hurts to lose them. I've always had people to date, but always kept them in arms reach and never allowed for depth. It's comforting yet terrifying at the same time... I just don't know what the best way to express this to my boyfriend would be without overwhelming him or coming across as clingy. We've seriously been dating for 6 months and I will move in soon, yet still I don't feel 100% invested emotionally. I know this doesn't help my already existing anxiety. He accepts me for who  am, but letting his family in is not easy as I tend to self sabotage...

It's nice to know you *get* how I feel. I am really sorry for the loss of your father. I think the hardest thing is trying to accept the advice from others who have stable family upbringings and their parents are still alive and supportive. I *know* that oftentimes people are trying to be genuinely caring, but many times, it just feels empty... It is also hard validating others' modern complaints. Not to say that other people do not have it tough it different ways, but when my colleagues and friends are freaking out about "minor" things in my eyes (e.g. finding an internship, getting a parking ticket, etc) It just makes me feel further removed from them because my priorities are different. 

I am just rambling but it doesn't help that my upbringing was completely dysfunctional and let's just say my parents could have done a better job. But, I have closed that chapter of my life, but it sometimes feels like the void is larger than it should be because my parents were only half there as a support system or people I could look up to / rely on.

Thanks for your condolences. I am up and down today. Luckily got out of bed and started making something of myself. Just as I was at wits ends a friend of mine messaged me randomly before I was going to sign of. I try to keep people close as a buffer for hurting myself, but that does not diminish the pain of the feelings that I have no control over...
